first_half#fh_1h_ot_note.description: KXNCAAMB1HSPREAD and KXNCAAMB1HTOTAL carry a secondary note 'Note: 2nd half markets are inclusive of overtime.' on first-half contracts, apparently a template carry-over; the primary text says 'in the 1st half' so overtime is taken as excluded, but the odd note is not explained.
first_half#fh_1h_ot_note.what_would_resolve: Kalshi contract terms for the 1H spread and total, or a settled game decided in overtime showing that first-half points alone were used.

first_half#fh_2h_tie.description: KXNCAAMB2H samples a 'wins the 2nd half' event but the equivalent 'tie in the 2nd half' contract (present for 1H) is not in the sample, so tie handling for 2H winners, and the effect of overtime periods on ties, is inferred.
first_half#fh_2h_tie.what_would_resolve: Fetch all contracts under one KXNCAAMB2H event ticker and read the rules for each outcome.

first_half#fh_halftime_infra.description: The size of the halftime update coefficient (how much of a first-half residual carries into the second half) is assumed to be small from general understanding of regression to the mean but is not measured here, and in-game feeds with timestamps are not verified as available at the break in time to trade.
first_half#fh_halftime_infra.what_would_resolve: Fit the 2H-on-1H regression on 5 seasons of half scores and check the latency of the ESPN live feed relative to Kalshi quotes during a game.

first_half#fh_opp_scheme_gap.description: Half-level opponent scheme effects (early press, rim-attack foul drawing in the first 10 minutes) cannot be built from free public data; only whole-game defensive style labels exist and may not apply to a half.
first_half#fh_opp_scheme_gap.what_would_resolve: Period-level tracking data (Synergy or Sportradar) for defensive play types by half, to test whether there is any half-specific matchup signal.

first_half#fh_postponement_text.description: Only KXNCAAMB1HWINNER states a postponement rule (two-week window); the sampled 1H, 1H spread, 1H total and 2H series have no postponement or fair-price clause, so whether the full-game 48-hour rule applies to them, or how a game halted at the break settles, is not visible.
first_half#fh_postponement_text.what_would_resolve: Full Kalshi terms for the half series or a historical postponed-game settlement for a half market.

futures_champion#fc_balance_hypothesis.description: The two-way balance profile is an empirical pattern in past champions, which could be the result of selection (top teams tend to be balanced) rather than an independent driver; with one champion per year the sample is small and the effect may not be distinguishable from noise.
futures_champion#fc_balance_hypothesis.what_would_resolve: A likelihood-ratio test over 20 or more tournaments of game-level outcomes (not only champions) using balance after controlling for rating.

futures_champion#fc_conf_bucket_rules.description: KXMARMADCONFWIN states no affiliation date or 'Other' definition, unlike KXNCAAMBCONF; for a team that changes conference between seasons, and for KXNCAAMBTOURNEY if the event is cancelled or ends without a final, settlement is not stated.
futures_champion#fc_conf_bucket_rules.what_would_resolve: Full Kalshi terms for KXMARMADCONFWIN and KXNCAAMBTOURNEY.

futures_champion#fc_coshare_payout.description: KXNCAAMBBIG10REG has no rules text; if it follows the KXNCAAMBBIGTENREG template it pays 1/N to declared co-champions, but this is inferred, and whether the Big Ten declares co-champions on tied records is conference policy not recorded here.
futures_champion#fc_coshare_payout.what_would_resolve: Rules text for KXNCAAMBBIG10REG and the Big Ten's published regular-season title policy.

futures_champion#fc_drift_calibration.description: The sd of change in team strength from November to March is stated as 2 to 3 points but is not estimated from data, and the dependence on roster continuity under the transfer portal is a recent phenomenon with few comparable seasons.
futures_champion#fc_drift_calibration.what_would_resolve: Fit the drift model on 12 seasons of weekly rating snapshots, stratified by returning minutes share, and report out-of-sample sd.

futures_champion#fc_r76_format.description: The 2027 NCAA field size is unverified (the KXMARMADROUND text, now in futures_seed_other, names a 'Round of 76'); an expanded field adds play-in games and changes how many wins a low seed needs for the title.
futures_champion#fc_r76_format.what_would_resolve: NCAA announcement of the 2027 tournament format, or the bracket structure on Selection Sunday.

futures_champion#fc_secondary_field_rule.description: The 2027 NIT and College Basketball Crown slot rules (which conferences feed which event, NET cut-offs, automatic places for regular-season champions) and their history of declined invitations were not verified; the NIT and Crown rules text names only the champion.
futures_champion#fc_secondary_field_rule.what_would_resolve: Published 2026-27 NIT and Crown selection procedures and past invitation/decline lists.

futures_champion#fc_title_only_series.description: KXMARMADREGION, KXNCAAMBHL, KXNCAAMBSUN and KXNCAAMBBIG10REG have no listing or rules text; their period, co-champion payout (for BIG10REG) and whether they duplicate futures_conference listings (HOR, ASUN, BIGTENREG) are not verified.
futures_champion#fc_title_only_series.what_would_resolve: A live listing or archived rules for each, compared with the duplicate futures_conference series.

futures_champion#fc_vacated_titles.description: None of the sampled national or conference championship rules say what happens if a champion is later vacated, disqualified or ruled ineligible, or by what date the champion is determined; in a world of eligibility litigation and revenue-sharing disputes this is not a negligible tail.
futures_champion#fc_vacated_titles.what_would_resolve: Kalshi's full terms for the series or a past case of a vacated result.

futures_champion#fc_womens_data.description: The women's title probability for KXNCAAMB2ML assumes possession-level women's box scores, NET history and bracket archives are scrapeable; field coverage, history depth and terms for stats.ncaa.org women's data and Her Hoop Stats were not checked.
futures_champion#fc_womens_data.what_would_resolve: Pull one season of women's box scores and NET snapshots from each source and confirm fields and history.

futures_conference#fcf_bans_vacated.description: No series says how a team under a postseason ban (eligible for a regular-season title but not the tournament), a vacated result, or a cancelled conference tournament settles; a cancelled tournament would leave QUAL and champion series without a winner.
futures_conference#fcf_bans_vacated.what_would_resolve: Kalshi rulebook provisions for cancelled events and a historical case (e.g. 2020 cancelled tournaments) showing settlement.

futures_conference#fcf_duplicates.description: Three tournaments are listed twice under different templates (IG12/BIG12, IGEAST/BIGEAST, IGTEN/BIG10) and BIG10REGTOP duplicates BIGTENREGTOP; whether the duplicates settle on identical terms, or one is a stale prior-season listing, is not established; KXNCAAMBWAC (sampled with Utah Valley, which leaves the WAC for the Big West in 2026-27) and KXNCAAMBUAC may be a prior-season and a current listing of one league after the WAC's announced rebrand as the United Athletic Conference (not verified).
futures_conference#fcf_duplicates.what_would_resolve: Compare market lists, dates and full rules of each duplicate pair for the same season.

futures_conference#fcf_non_d1_counting.description: The regular-season series do not say how standings are ordered when teams play unequal numbers of conference games after cancellations (win percentage or wins), nor whether a forfeit counts as a conference result; REGTOP compares 'identical win-loss records' only.
futures_conference#fcf_non_d1_counting.what_would_resolve: Kalshi's full terms for REG/REGTOP or a past settlement in a season with unequal conference game counts.

futures_conference#fcf_policy_source.description: Per-conference co-champion declaration policies and tournament tiebreak manuals are assumed to be published on conference websites for all leagues; coverage and versioning were not checked.
futures_conference#fcf_policy_source.what_would_resolve: Collect the 2026-27 championship manuals for the ACC, Big Ten, Big 12, Big East, SEC and a sample of one-bid leagues.

futures_conference#fcf_rank_basis.description: The top-finisher rules break ties only among teams with identical conference win-loss records but do not say how non-identical records are ordered (wins, win percentage or losses) when teams play unequal numbers of conference games after cancellations or unbalanced alignments.
futures_conference#fcf_rank_basis.what_would_resolve: Kalshi contract terms or a settled case with unequal conference game counts showing which ordering decided the finish.

futures_conference#fcf_strength_sd.description: The sd of the shared strength factor (assumed about 2 to 3 points early, declining with games) sets the dispersion of conference records and therefore tie frequencies and top-N tails, but is not estimated for post-realignment leagues.
futures_conference#fcf_strength_sd.what_would_resolve: Fit strength-sd by games played on 15 seasons of rating snapshots and compare simulated co-champion frequencies with history.

futures_conference#fcf_tiebreak_schedule.description: New conference alignments and unbalanced schedules mean there is little or no history on how teams behave in the final games of schedules with mismatched numbers of home and away meetings, and the effort effect after clinching has not been measured on this structure.
futures_conference#fcf_tiebreak_schedule.what_would_resolve: Two or more seasons of data under the new alignments, or analogous history from unbalanced conferences (Big Ten, ACC), to estimate leverage effects.

futures_seed_other#so_committee_subjecti.description: The committee's chair, member composition and recusal rules change each year and its judgement on injuries and eye-test quality is not systematised; the noise sd of two to four slots is an estimate from few seasons under the NET regime and might be larger.
futures_seed_other#so_committee_subjecti.what_would_resolve: Fit the ordered probit across 2018 to 2026 with year-level random effects and report the committee noise and its stability.

futures_seed_other#so_field_size.description: KXMARMADROUND names a 'Round of 76', which does not match a 68-team field; the 2027 format (field size, number of play-in games, which seed lines play in) changes at-large counts, bubble probabilities and the round labels the other series use.
futures_seed_other#so_field_size.what_would_resolve: NCAA announcement of the 2027 tournament format and the KXMARMADROUND market list.

futures_seed_other#so_no_series.description: KXMARMADHIGHSEED has no listing or rules text; for the bracket-statistic series the text does not say whether First Four games count toward 'the full tournament' (SEEDDIF) or whether a First Four winner's official seed is the line it plays on (SEEDSUM).
futures_seed_other#so_no_series.what_would_resolve: Full Kalshi terms for SEEDDIF, SEEDSUM and a HIGHSEED listing, or a past settlement involving a First Four team.

futures_seed_other#so_regular_season_cou.description: KXNCAAMBWINS and KXNCAAMBUNDEFEATED count 'official regular season games as defined by the league's governing body' but do not say whether games against non-Division I opponents or exempt-event games count; ESPN and NCAA records can differ on non-D1 games, which changes the counted games and the feasibility of high strikes.
futures_seed_other#so_regular_season_cou.what_would_resolve: Kalshi's full terms for KXNCAAMBWINS or a past settlement for a team with a non-D1 game.

futures_seed_other#so_source_access.description: Scrape access and history depth for NCAA NET and team sheets, WarrenNolan archived sheets and the Bracket Matrix archive were assumed; NET exists only from 2018-19 so the ordinal model has about seven usable tournaments (2020 cancelled) under changing quadrant rules.
futures_seed_other#so_source_access.what_would_resolve: Confirm each source's fields, archive depth and terms, and count usable seasons per quadrant-rule vintage before fitting.

futures_seed_other#so_team_sheet_access.description: The committee's own team sheets are available to members through an evaluation tool but not publicly; public reconstructions (WarrenNolan, ESPN) may differ on quadrant definitions and exclude some metrics, so the inputs to the revealed-preference fit are approximations of what the committee saw.
futures_seed_other#so_team_sheet_access.what_would_resolve: Compare reconstructed sheets with the NCAA's published team sheets released after Selection Sunday for a few seasons and quantify differences.

game_moneyline_spread#ml_avail_gap.description: College basketball has no league-mandated injury report with timestamps, so the timing of undisclosed absences relative to Kalshi close is not recoverable from free sources; the lineup-adjusted rating can only be backtested with after-the-fact box scores.
game_moneyline_spread#ml_avail_gap.what_would_resolve: Own timestamped capture of team and beat-writer posts for a season, or a paid feed with status timestamps (SOURCE_UNVERIFIED which vendors have it).

game_moneyline_spread#ml_d3_ratings.description: KXNCAAMBD3GAME pairs two Division III teams; the D3 rating defined here is a margin-only fit on a sparse graph with no possession or availability data, and its out-of-sample margin error (and whether an 11-point game sd applies to D3) is unmeasured.
game_moneyline_spread#ml_d3_ratings.what_would_resolve: Backtest the D3 margin rating over five seasons of D3 results and compare its margin RMSE and calibration with Massey D3 ratings.

game_moneyline_spread#ml_fair_price.description: Every series resolves a cancelled or out-of-window game 'to a fair price' (D3GAME adds 'in accordance with the rules') but no sampled text says how the fair price is computed, and KXNCAAMBSGP has no postponement clause at all.
game_moneyline_spread#ml_fair_price.what_would_resolve: Kalshi's full contract terms for these series or a historical cancelled-game settlement showing the payout used.

game_moneyline_spread#ml_luck_wiring.description: Three-point luck and free-throw luck are catalog inputs that are not wired to this archetype; it is unclear whether the rating ensemble's shrinkage already handles them, which affects whether a separate luck term is a double count.
game_moneyline_spread#ml_luck_wiring.what_would_resolve: Compare out-of-sample margin error of ratings with and without an explicit opponent-3P%-luck term in a held-out season.

game_moneyline_spread#ml_ot_in_margin.description: None of the sampled full-game rules (spread, winning margin, parlay) states whether overtime points count toward the margin; the 2nd-half markets spell it out and the full-game ones only say 'official final result'. If OT is excluded, a tied-at-regulation game is a push-like void rather than a 1 to 6 point margin.
game_moneyline_spread#ml_ot_in_margin.what_would_resolve: The full rules text of KXNCAAMBGAME/KXNCAAMBSPREAD from Kalshi's contract terms PDF, or a historical OT game's settlement showing which margin was used.

game_moneyline_spread#ml_source_access.description: ESPN injuries pages and Bart Torvik player tables are named as availability and player-impact sources, and Torvik time-machine coverage of prior seasons is assumed; none of the field coverage, history depth or terms of use was checked for this record.
game_moneyline_spread#ml_source_access.what_would_resolve: Pull a sample of 50 non-power-conference games per source and confirm status fields, timestamps and history depth, or buy a licensed feed.

game_total#tot_apl_source.description: Average possession length by team (offence and defence) is believed to be published by KenPom (paid) and possibly Torvik, but I did not verify the field names or whether a point-in-time history exists, and the possession-length model depends on it.
game_total#tot_apl_source.what_would_resolve: Fetch a KenPom team page or Torvik team table and confirm the field, plus a historical snapshot availability check.

game_total#tot_base_rates.description: The overtime frequency (about 5 to 6 percent of games), the combined points an overtime period adds (earlier drafts said 10 to 12, which is below pace arithmetic of about 15 to 18) and the tie-chain probabilities are stated from general knowledge with no measured source in this record.
game_total#tot_base_rates.what_would_resolve: Compute the rates from several seasons of Division I box-score line scores (overtime flag, period points) and replace the quoted figures with the measured values and their intervals.

game_total#tot_crew_timing.description: Officiating crews for most college games are not published until close to game day, so a crew effect cannot be used in the tradable window; the size of the crew effect on totals is unproven for college.
game_total#tot_crew_timing.what_would_resolve: A season of assignment timestamps from conferences or KenPom, and a regression of crew foul-rate on game FT attempts out of sample.

game_total#tot_ot_inclusion.description: The sampled KXNCAAMBTOTAL rules say 'over 126.5 total points are scored' and defer to the official final result but never say overtime points count; the 2nd-half series state 'inclusive of overtime' explicitly, which suggests the full-game total includes OT yet this is inferred.
game_total#tot_ot_inclusion.what_would_resolve: Kalshi's full contract terms for the NCAA men's basketball total, or a past game that went to overtime and its settlement value.

game_total#tot_source_access.description: Access to Torvik player on/off data for the handler-absence pace shift and to KenPom referee ratings (coverage, timing, licence) was not verified for this record.
game_total#tot_source_access.what_would_resolve: Sample both sources for 50 games, confirm the fields, history depth and terms, or fall back to own play-by-play lineup reconstruction.

player_points#pp_disclosure.description: College programmes do not release official injury reports, so the pre-tip probability that a starter plays is mostly hidden; no free dataset records when a status became public, which prevents a time-stamped backtest of the DNP scenario weight.
player_points#pp_disclosure.what_would_resolve: A season of own-captured team posts with timestamps or a vendor that records status timestamps (SOURCE_UNVERIFIED).

player_points#pp_pbp_timing.description: Whether ESPN or NCAA play-by-play records the clock and score of every scoring event, and so supports first-to-10/25/50 timing, for lower-division and non-televised games was not verified; the race profile (now used by unreg:race_to_n_points) and the late-foul timing used here depend on it.
player_points#pp_pbp_timing.what_would_resolve: Pull play-by-play for 30 non-televised Division I games, check scoring-event timestamps and running score, and confirm bulk access terms.

player_points#pp_race_who.description: The four 'Race to N Points' series were the only live series under this key and were moved to unreg:race_to_n_points by the reconciliation; whether the racing entity is a team or a player, tie handling and a game ending before N were never verified, and this record no longer prices them.
player_points#pp_race_who.what_would_resolve: Read KXNCAAMBFIRST25 rules in the unreg:race_to_n_points review; re-open this archetype only if a per-player points series is listed.

player_points#pp_settlement_unknown.description: No rules text was sampled for any live series, and no per-player points ladder appears in the ledger, so DNP handling (void versus NO), OT inclusion, rung construction and the stat source for a points prop are all unknown; every availability and minutes input depends on this.
player_points#pp_settlement_unknown.what_would_resolve: Read rules_primary and rules_secondary for the Kalshi men's college basketball player points series (if listed) and for a DNP case in the NBA analogue.

player_points#pp_shot_source.description: I believe hoop-math.com provides shot-location splits by player for D1, but I did not verify its current coverage, export format or whether it covers the 2026-27 season; the xPPS input depends on it.
player_points#pp_shot_source.what_would_resolve: Fetch a player page from hoop-math.com and a team defence page and confirm the fields and the latest season available.

player_props#pr_cold_start_calibration.description: The translation factors from prior-team usage and rate to the new team (conference-tier discount, minutes vacated pass-through) are stated as plausible magnitudes but not calibrated, and the portal era has too few seasons to separate role change from selection into transferring.
player_props#pr_cold_start_calibration.what_would_resolve: Fit the translation on all D1 transfers since 2021 with out-of-sample prediction of first-10-game minutes and usage.

player_props#pr_disclosure_timing.description: College availability information has no timestamped official source, so the cause-specific appearance probabilities cannot be backtested at the moment a trader would act; only post-game rosters are reliable.
player_props#pr_disclosure_timing.what_would_resolve: One season of captured status posts with timestamps, or a vendor providing historical status vintage (none verified).

player_props#pr_no_contract.description: The ledger has no live Kalshi series for generic men's college basketball player props, so no rules text exists to establish DNP handling, overtime, stat provider, combination definitions or rung construction; the whole archetype is defined only by the catalog's description and the contract cannot be reviewed.
player_props#pr_no_contract.what_would_resolve: A live or past Kalshi college basketball player-prop series to sample, or confirmation from Kalshi that none is offered.

player_props#pr_scorekeeper_effect.description: The home scorekeeper effect on assists and blocks is documented in professional basketball but I have not verified its existence or size in college, where statisticians vary by school; the input could be near zero outside a few venues.
player_props#pr_scorekeeper_effect.what_would_resolve: Compute home-minus-away assist rates by venue from 3 seasons of Sports-Reference game logs and test dispersion across venues against a null of equal gaps.

player_props#pr_source_access.description: ESPN injury pages for men's college basketball and EvanMiya player-rating pricing and coverage are named as sources but neither the NCAAM injury coverage nor the EvanMiya subscription terms and fields were checked; the home-scorekeeper effect is already flagged separately.
player_props#pr_source_access.what_would_resolve: Sample 50 Division I games for ESPN injury-page coverage and obtain EvanMiya's current terms and exportable fields, or substitute own capture.

player_rebounds_assists#ra_no_contract.description: There is no live Kalshi series for college player rebounds or assists in the ledger, so nothing about DNP handling, overtime, the statistician source or combination definitions is observable; the archetype is defined only by the catalog text.
player_rebounds_assists#ra_no_contract.what_would_resolve: A sample of a live Kalshi rebounds or assists series for men's college basketball, or confirmation that none exists.

player_rebounds_assists#ra_numeric_assum.description: Several numbers in the record are assumptions without a source: correlation of about 0.5 between assists and team made shots, a rebound pool of 60 to 70 with sd near 7, and the +0.6 and -0.5 shooting-shock loadings (the loadings are also flagged in ra_shock_loading).
player_rebounds_assists#ra_numeric_assum.what_would_resolve: Estimate each from several seasons of Division I box scores (team makes vs assists, rebound pool by game) and replace the assumed figures with measured values.

player_rebounds_assists#ra_scorer_discre.description: The size of scorer discretion on assists across college venues is not verified; if material it adds a venue-specific bias to any assist prop that no attached input captures, and whether a free dataset reveals it is unknown.
player_rebounds_assists#ra_scorer_discre.what_would_resolve: Compare home and away assist rates by venue over three seasons from public game logs and test whether between-venue variance exceeds the null.

player_rebounds_assists#ra_shock_loading.description: The loadings of the shared shooting shock on rebounds and assists (assumed about +0.6 and -0.5 for guards) are plausible by construction but not estimated; the magnitude determines combination-prop pricing and the correlation between guard assists and team rebounds.
player_rebounds_assists#ra_shock_loading.what_would_resolve: Estimate the one-factor loadings on three seasons of game logs by role and report their sampling error.

player_rebounds_assists#ra_source_access.description: Public availability of assisted-share and rebound-by-location data (hoop-math, ESPN play-by-play), Torvik lineup data and ESPN roster height and position fields was not verified for current seasons or for non-televised games.
player_rebounds_assists#ra_source_access.what_would_resolve: Sample each source for 30 games and confirm the fields, history depth and terms before building the inputs on them.

player_rebounds_assists#ra_tracking_gap.description: Potential assists, rebound positioning (box-outs, contested rebounds) and pick-and-roll initiation are tracking data held by Synergy, Sportradar or the programmes; public sources only report the outcomes, so creation share and true rebound positioning must be inferred from counts.
player_rebounds_assists#ra_tracking_gap.what_would_resolve: A licence for tracking data on a sample of games to check how much of creation share is captured by assist and turnover counts alone.

player_threes#th_no_contract.description: No live Kalshi series for single-game college three-pointers made exists in the ledger, so DNP handling, overtime, rung construction and provider are all undefined; the only three-point-related live series is the season stat leader, which is a different contract.
player_threes#th_no_contract.what_would_resolve: A sample of a live or past Kalshi college basketball threes-made market and its rules text, or confirmation that none exists.

player_threes#th_persistence_claim.description: The claim that opponent three-point attempts conceded persists (correlation about 0.5) while percentage allowed does not is based on general understanding of basketball analytics and was not verified on college data, and the 0.6 and 0.1 weights in the matchup input are assumptions.
player_threes#th_persistence_claim.what_would_resolve: Compute split-half and season-to-season correlations of 3PA allowed rate and 3P% allowed across D1 teams over at least five seasons.

player_threes#th_source_access.description: Whether ESPN play-by-play flags assisted shots for all Division I games, whether hoop-math three-point splits are current, and how far back Bart Torvik three-point-rate-allowed series run were not verified.
player_threes#th_source_access.what_would_resolve: Sample 50 games from each source for assisted flags and zone fields and check the series start years.

player_threes#th_tracking_gap.description: Defender distance, open versus contested labels and catch-and-shoot flags are tracking data held by Synergy or Sportradar; public play-by-play only provides assisted or unassisted, so open-look quality is approximated.
player_threes#th_tracking_gap.what_would_resolve: A licence for a tracking sample to test how much of shot quality is explained by the assisted flag and zone alone.

player_threes#th_trailing_magnitude.description: The size of the trailing-team attempt lift (assumed 15 to 30 percent late in games) is not measured and depends on coaching habits; it may be much smaller for stretch bigs, who shoot threes regardless of state.
player_threes#th_trailing_magnitude.what_would_resolve: Estimate attempt share by lead and time bins from two seasons of play-by-play and compare by player role.

team_total#tt_env_gap.description: Venue (cbb.venue, cbb.neutral_site) is now an input, but the size of the home-versus-neutral shift in one team's own points as against the margin, and whether it is team specific, is not established; the roughly half-of-margin split is an assumption.
team_total#tt_env_gap.what_would_resolve: Estimate home minus neutral offensive rating by team over 3 seasons with shrinkage and test whether it adds out-of-sample power over a common home effect.

team_total#tt_joint_pricing.description: The two teams' ladders in one game are linked through the total and the margin; the right correlation structure between home and away points (positive through pace, negative through blowout shape) is only approximated by the coupling input and not validated across spread buckets.
team_total#tt_joint_pricing.what_would_resolve: A fit of the bivariate distribution of (home points, away points) by expected-margin bucket on 8 seasons and a check against the sum constraint with the game total.

team_total#tt_mostpts_scope.description: The KXNCAAMBTEAMMOSTPTS text does not say whether overtime points count toward 'the most points', what happens if a game in the round is not played or forfeited, or whether First Four games belong to the Round of 64 for this purpose.
team_total#tt_mostpts_scope.what_would_resolve: Kalshi's full terms for KXNCAAMBTEAMMOSTPTS or a past settlement of a round containing an overtime game.

team_total#tt_ot_scope.description: The rules sample does not say whether a team's overtime points count; with a ladder up to 90-plus points the OT mixture changes upper-tail probabilities noticeably, and the label could differ if a provider reports regulation-only points.
team_total#tt_ot_scope.what_would_resolve: Kalshi full terms or a historical overtime game with the final settlement value for a team-total strike near the regulation score.

team_total#tt_scheme_data.description: Zone and press frequencies per team are available from licensed tracking (Synergy) but I could not verify any free public source that reports them by team and season, so the defence-style input may be limited to coarse labels.
team_total#tt_scheme_data.what_would_resolve: Check Torvik, KenPom and Sports-Reference for a zone or press share field; otherwise attempt scheme classification from play-by-play.

unreg:coaching_and_governance_events#coa.description: The rules do not define when a coach is 'selected' (reported agreement, university announcement, board approval or signed contract) nor the resolution source, which matters for hires near the Sep 1, 2027 cutoff and for interim-to-permanent conversions.
unreg:coaching_and_governance_events#coa.what_would_resolve: Kalshi clarification or a past settled next-coach market showing which event and source fixed the outcome.

unreg:coaching_and_governance_events#coa.description: No input models simultaneous competing vacancies (other schools hiring in the same cycle) that bid for the same candidates; a rival opening at a higher-resourced school can take a candidate off the board.
unreg:coaching_and_governance_events#coa.what_would_resolve: Build a cycle-level vacancy table with school resources and link overlaps, then estimate candidate loss rates to rival openings.

unreg:coaching_and_governance_events#coa.description: Report-to-hire conversion rates by outlet and stage have not been measured; historical insider posts on X are hard to capture with original timestamps and some reports were deleted.
unreg:coaching_and_governance_events#coa.what_would_resolve: Reconstruct at least five past cycles from archived articles and timestamped posts, and check coverage against a sample of known hires.

unreg:coaching_and_governance_events#coa.description: Revenue-sharing budgets after the 2025 House settlement are new; their weight in candidate decisions relative to salary and ties has no historical analogue in pre-2025 searches.
unreg:coaching_and_governance_events#coa.what_would_resolve: Track 2026 and 2027 cycles with reported roster budgets and compare hire patterns with pre-2025 cycles.

unreg:coaching_and_governance_events#coa.description: The interim-to-permanent base rate needs a list of past D1 interim head coaches with spans and outcomes; no structured public table is known, and Stadium's current college-basketball insider coverage and whether ESPN public JSON exposes search reports with original timestamps are also unverified.
unreg:coaching_and_governance_events#coa.what_would_resolve: Hand-compile interim seasons from press releases and Wikipedia and test the sample size; check which outlets still publish insider coverage and whether ESPN's news endpoint carries timestamped items.

unreg:kenpom_rating_snapshot#kp_algo.description: KenPom's exact update weights, recency treatment and blowout handling are not public; the claim that margins have diminishing returns and a 1/g weight is a modelling belief that needs calibration on stored daily snapshots.
unreg:kenpom_rating_snapshot#kp_algo.what_would_resolve: Fit the update rule on stored snapshots and confirm RMSE against actual next-day ratings, or documentation from KenPom's methodology pages.

unreg:kenpom_rating_snapshot#kp_exact_ra.description: Only a #1 and a top-25 contract were sampled; other exact rank slots, tie display rules and the behaviour if the site is down at the timestamp are not visible in the sample.
unreg:kenpom_rating_snapshot#kp_exact_ra.what_would_resolve: A listing of all open KXNCAAMBKENPOMRANK strikes plus the full rule text.

unreg:kenpom_rating_snapshot#kp_prior_sc.description: The schedule on which KenPom phases out its preseason prior during the 2026-27 season (date fully removed, functional form) is not verified, and it drives early-season rank volatility in cbb.kenpom_prior_drift.
unreg:kenpom_rating_snapshot#kp_prior_sc.what_would_resolve: KenPom's methodology posts for the current season, or fit prior weight from the gap between KenPom and a results-only replica over past seasons.

unreg:kenpom_rating_snapshot#kp_source_a.description: Whether the KenPom main ratings table (rank, AdjEM, AdjO, AdjD, AdjT) is free to view and whether the dated ratings archive is subscriber-only could not be checked here: the site is unreachable from this environment.
unreg:kenpom_rating_snapshot#kp_source_a.what_would_resolve: Load kenpom.com logged out and logged in, confirm which fields are visible, and confirm archive access and terms for automated capture.

unreg:kenpom_rating_snapshot#kp_tz.description: The sampled rules state 12:00pm EST for Monday Mar 15, 2027, the day after the US switch to daylight time and after Selection Sunday; they do not say whether this is fixed-offset EST or New York local time, nor how a mid-refresh or unavailable page is treated.
unreg:kenpom_rating_snapshot#kp_tz.what_would_resolve: Kalshi's full contract terms or a past settled KenPom snapshot market showing which page capture was used.

unreg:overtime_periods#ot_u1.description: The rules do not say how a game halted during overtime counts toward 'periods played', which provider supplies the official result, or how the 'fair price' on cancellation is computed.
unreg:overtime_periods#ot_u1.what_would_resolve: Kalshi clarification or inspection of a settled KXNCAAMBOT market with a suspended or cancelled game.

unreg:overtime_periods#ot_u2.description: Unclear whether fatigue in multi-team-event weekends, back-to-back days or high-stakes games changes end-game risk appetite or repeat-tie rates; with roughly 6 percent of games reaching OT, the 2+ subsample is too small to learn this without pooling.
unreg:overtime_periods#ot_u2.what_would_resolve: Hierarchical model of OT-period tie rates with rest-days and event-type covariates on 15+ seasons of OT periods.

unreg:overtime_periods#ot_u3.description: The foul-carryover input assumes the men's game uses two halves, a five-foul limit and team-foul bonus carrying into overtime; any rules-committee change (such as a move to quarters, already made in the women's game) would change per-period tie rates.
unreg:overtime_periods#ot_u3.what_would_resolve: Confirm the 2026-27 NCAA men's playing rules for period structure, bonus and foul carryover.

unreg:overtime_periods#ot_u4.description: It is undecided whether SIFT prices KXNCAAMBOT in play; the sampled market is a finalized per-game ladder and the rungs are close to zero until a late tie, so a pregame-only model prices almost nothing useful after tip. The free live feed's latency and field completeness are unverified.
unreg:overtime_periods#ot_u4.what_would_resolve: Decide the pricing scope (pregame only or in play) and, if in play, measure ESPN live-feed latency against a licensed feed on a sample of games.

unreg:overtime_periods#ot_u5.description: Only the 3+ rung of KXNCAAMBOT (floor_strike 2.5) has sampled rules text; whether 1+ and 2+ rungs exist and how their strikes and wording read is inferred, and claims about rung nesting stay conditional on that.
unreg:overtime_periods#ot_u5.what_would_resolve: Sample rules text and floor_strike of the other KXNCAAMBOT rungs (tickers ending -1, -2) from the Kalshi archive.

unreg:polls_and_awards#pa_ap_ties_and_da.description: AP polls sometimes list ties for a rank (two teams share a position) and the 'expected' Final poll date of Apr 6, 2027 can move; the rank-specific series (for example #3) do not say how a tied rank resolves or what happens if the Final Rankings are released on a different date.
unreg:polls_and_awards#pa_ap_ties_and_da.what_would_resolve: Kalshi's full rule text for the AP rank series and a historical example of a tied rank in the AP Final poll.

unreg:polls_and_awards#pa_award_criteria.description: KXNCAAMBMOP, KXNCAAMBNAISMITH and KXNCAAMBCOTY state no co-winner or non-play rule (only AWARD and CONFAWARD do), and KXNCAAMBAWARD may cover awards other than the sampled Tournament MOP, so whether MOP and AWARD settle identically is not established.
unreg:polls_and_awards#pa_award_criteria.what_would_resolve: Full Kalshi terms for MOP, NAISMITH and COTY, and the market list of KXNCAAMBAWARD for one season.

unreg:polls_and_awards#pa_ballot_access.description: I believe the AP publishes each voter's ballot every week but did not verify that historical ballots are accessible in bulk or how far back; the voter-level model depends on it.
unreg:polls_and_awards#pa_ballot_access.what_would_resolve: Check the AP Top 25 page for a past week's ballot list and test scraping for 5 seasons.

unreg:polls_and_awards#pa_churn_base_rat.description: The base rate of changes at #1 and the successor rule are assumed to be driven by losses and leapfrogs, but I did not compute the historical distribution of distinct #1 counts or the leapfrog share; the threshold of 9 is large relative to my expectation and may mostly reflect a priced tail.
unreg:polls_and_awards#pa_churn_base_rat.what_would_resolve: Compute the distinct-#1 count for each season from 2000 to 2026 from AP archives and fit the transition model to it.

unreg:polls_and_awards#pa_coach_model.description: The coach-of-the-year over-performance model is fitted on a small sample (one winner per year) and voter preferences (turnarounds, conference titles, tournament runs) shift; the Naismith vote timing relative to the tournament is not verified.
unreg:polls_and_awards#pa_coach_model.what_would_resolve: Collect 20 seasons of Naismith and AP COTY finalists with preseason expectations and test the multinomial fit out of sample.

unreg:polls_and_awards#pa_source_access.description: Scrapeability and leaderboard history of stats.ncaa.org and the availability of AP poll points totals in Sports-Reference poll-history pages were not verified (AP ballot access is flagged separately).
unreg:polls_and_awards#pa_source_access.what_would_resolve: Fetch five seasons of NCAA leaderboards and AP poll histories and confirm fields, depth and terms of use.

unreg:race_to_n_points#race_close_time.description: The evidence does not show whether KXNCAAMBRACE markets close at tip or keep trading in play; this decides whether cbb.race_live_state and a live feed are required or unused.
unreg:race_to_n_points#race_close_time.what_would_resolve: Market close_time versus scheduled tip from the Kalshi API for a sample of KXNCAAMBRACE markets.

unreg:race_to_n_points#race_first_clause.description: The KXNCAAMBFIRST10/25/50 samples contain no postponement or cancellation clause, and no series sample says whether overtime counts or how a game where neither team reaches N (plausible only for N=50) settles.
unreg:race_to_n_points#race_first_clause.what_would_resolve: Full contract terms for both series generations, or a settled N=50 market from a game that ended below 50.

unreg:race_to_n_points#race_pbp_source.description: Free play-by-play sources for college basketball are inconsistent in time stamps and possession flags, and tip-winner fields may not exist; the claim of a measurable opening-possession edge needs verification.
unreg:race_to_n_points#race_pbp_source.what_would_resolve: Pull a sample of 500 games from ESPN and the NCAA feed and test whether first-possession and scoring order are reliably recoverable.

unreg:race_to_n_points#race_seq_correcti.description: How often the official scoring sequence is corrected after the game (scorer changes that move a basket between teams or alter points) is unknown, and that is the only route to a disputed order.
unreg:race_to_n_points#race_seq_correcti.what_would_resolve: Compare live and final play-by-play for several hundred games and count sequence changes near N=10, 25 and 50.

unreg:season_stat_leader#sl_categories.description: Only a points-per-game conference market and a made-threes national market were sampled; other categories (rebounds, assists, steals, blocks) and their qualification rules may exist with different drivers.
unreg:season_stat_leader#sl_categories.what_would_resolve: A full listing of open strikes by category in both series.

unreg:season_stat_leader#sl_conf_table.description: For KXNCAAMBCONFLEADER the rules say 'the most points per game in the Southeastern Conference' but the visible text does not say whether the NCAA table filtered to the conference or the conference office's table, with its own minimum, settles.
unreg:season_stat_leader#sl_conf_table.what_would_resolve: The truncated rules text, or a settled conference-leader market where the two tables differed.

unreg:season_stat_leader#sl_invitational.description: Participation in the College Basketball Crown, CBI and CIT is by invitation and team choice, and the 2026-27 fields and formats are not known, so postseason game counts for mid-ranked teams are uncertain.
unreg:season_stat_leader#sl_invitational.what_would_resolve: Announced 2026-27 formats and historical acceptance rates of eligible non-NIT teams by rating rank.

unreg:season_stat_leader#sl_ncaa_min.description: The exact NCAA minimum thresholds per statistic (share of games or minimum totals) and how postseason games, including non-NCAA events such as the College Basketball Crown, enter the official table are not verified here.
unreg:season_stat_leader#sl_ncaa_min.what_would_resolve: The NCAA statistics policy document for 2026-27 and a check of past final tables for NIT, CBI and Crown inclusion.

unreg:season_stat_leader#sl_truncated.description: The sampled rules_secondary text is truncated at 'If Zoom Diallo does not', so the rule for a player who does not qualify, does not play, or ties for the lead, and the named source of truth, are not visible.
unreg:season_stat_leader#sl_truncated.what_would_resolve: Full rules text for both series from the Kalshi API or contract terms.

unreg:tournament_player_milestone#mile_u.description: Rules do not name the official stat source, the cut-off for post-game stat corrections, or state explicitly that overtime statistics count; a corrected rebound or assist can turn a 9 into a 10.
unreg:tournament_player_milestone#mile_u.what_would_resolve: Kalshi clarification of the data source and correction policy, or a settled precedent involving a stat correction.

unreg:tournament_player_milestone#mile_u.description: Effects of neutral tournament venues (dome sightlines on shooting, neutral official scorers on assist and rebound recording) on far-tail stat lines are not measured; the samples of tournament 40+ point games and triple-doubles are very small.
unreg:tournament_player_milestone#mile_u.what_would_resolve: Pool tournament and neutral-site regular-season games over 15+ seasons and estimate venue shifts in three-point percentage and assist/rebound recording.

unreg:tournament_player_milestone#mile_u.description: Field format for the 2027 tournament may differ from 68 teams (another series references a Round of 76); the number of play-in games and team-games per tournament changes exposure and must be confirmed before pricing a 2027 series.
unreg:tournament_player_milestone#mile_u.what_would_resolve: Official NCAA announcement of the 2027 men's tournament field size and play-in structure.

unreg:tournament_player_milestone#mile_u.description: Far-tail calibration rests on very few events (50-point tournament games and tournament triple-doubles are rare across decades), so per-player tail models are extrapolations whose error dominates the estimate.
unreg:tournament_player_milestone#mile_u.what_would_resolve: Validate tail models on all D1 regular-season 45+ point games and triple-doubles, checking predicted versus observed counts by role and usage band.

unreg:tournament_player_milestone#mile_u.description: Complete player-game box scores for early tournaments (blocks and steals were not officially recorded before the late 1980s) and the exact counts of 50-point games and triple-doubles per tournament are not in the sampled material; the base-rate anchor cannot be quantified here and no counts are asserted.
unreg:tournament_player_milestone#mile_u.what_would_resolve: Compile qualifying events from NCAA records and Sports-Reference tournament pages for 1985 to present, and verify box-score completeness per year.

unreg:tournament_player_milestone#mile_u.description: Sports-Reference's player game finder for triple-doubles appears to sit behind the paid Stathead product, and its college player game logs may start only around 2010-11; Barttorvik and hoopR player-game completeness for older seasons is also unchecked. The effect of neutral-site scorekeepers on recorded stats is likewise unmeasured.
unreg:tournament_player_milestone#mile_u.what_would_resolve: Check Stathead access and the first season with player game logs in each free source, and test box-score completeness on a sample of tournament games per season.
